designedAgainst.prerequisiteLevelStatus: reconciled — b1.md/b1.json merged after this blueprint's first draft and every b1.* id below was updated to match the real B1 capability graph; the full structural LC-AUD-001 cross-level audit is still pending
designedAgainst.note: Design only. No runtime module imports this file; nothing here is available to a learner.

canDo: develop and defend an opinion on an everyday-but-real issue, with reasons, and hold it under a genuine counter-argument
weigh several options against each other and recommend one, stating the trade-offs
handle something going wrong by explaining the problem, justifying a request, and negotiating a resolution, including under pushback
reason about the unreal: hypothesize about a different present/future, speculate about cause and effect, express regret about a past decision
mediate language for somebody else: summarize a conversation or text, reformulate for clarity, report a third person's opinion
read and use register: adjust formality, soften or strengthen a statement on purpose, catch an implied meaning
sustain a long, multi-topic conversation, follow a topic change, and reach an agreement after more than one objection
cannotYet: produce a structured, sustained monologue (a prepared presentation) as a primary skill
argue academic or highly abstract positions rather than concrete everyday-real issues
use idiom as a first-class productive skill (recognition and light use only)
reformulate with stylistic nuance rather than clarity as the goal
have pragmatic appropriateness graded as the primary criterion for every capability, rather than only where arc 5/6 specifically need it
produce or receive formal written correspondence (letters/emails) as its own genre
definition.interactionCeiling: single-topic exchanges of 9-12 meaningful turns per arc 1-5, rising to a 16-20 turn multi-topic capstone conversation in arc 6, with repair available throughout and support fading by evidence

b1Inheritance.note: Reconciled against the real docs/curriculum/blueprints/b1.md / b1.json, which merged to main after this blueprint's first draft. b1.* ids below are real B1 capability ids, not placeholders. A full structural LC-AUD-001 cross-level audit is still required before runtime content depends on this document, but these ids are no longer guesses.

relatedButNotPrerequisite.note: B1 capabilities close enough to a B2 capability that this blueprint had to prove genuine escalation rather than duplication (master contract section 17, 'no duplicated new capability already taught earlier').
relatedButNotPrerequisite.b1.negotiate_a_solution: B2's negotiate_a_resolution/negotiate_an_agreement_under_pushback extend this to justification-grounded requests and multiple rounds of objection, not a re-teach of single-round negotiation.
relatedButNotPrerequisite.b1.express_frustration_politely: should-scope in B1. B2's express_frustration_diplomatically adds hedged, register-aware diplomacy under a live negotiation rather than the flat-politeness tone layer B1 teaches.
relatedButNotPrerequisite.b1.summarize_what_was_said: should-scope in B1, and same-conversation/same-audience recap. B2's summarize_for_someone_else is the CEFR mediation move proper: a summary for a third party who was not present.
relatedButNotPrerequisite.b1.compare_options_with_reasons: B2's weigh_advantages_and_disadvantages requires the trade-off named explicitly (advantage_disadvantage_frame) as its own discourse move, not only a justified choice.
relatedButNotPrerequisite.b1.recommend_or_warn: should-scope in B1. B2's weigh_advantages_and_disadvantages is required and adds the explicit trade-off frame; a B2 learner may recommend without ever having had recommend_or_warn evidenced.
relatedButNotPrerequisite.b1.talk_about_real_conditions: should-scope in B1 (first conditional). Gives a head start toward hypothesize_about_unreal_situations but cannot be a hard prerequisite since it is not guaranteed for every learner.
relatedButNotPrerequisite.b1.imagine_a_hypothetical: optional-scope in B1, explicitly described there as 'a light preview of B2's hypothetical reasoning, kept to one fixed frame.' hypothesize_about_unreal_situations is the capability that preview points to; still not a hard prerequisite for the same reason.

canDos.why: The next step past b1.give_an_opinion: not just stating a reason, but sustaining the position under a genuine counter-argument, which is the discourse-level demand B2 must add.
transferContexts: a novel everyday issue not used during teaching

canDos.why: b1.compare_options_with_reasons stops at a justified choice; B1's should-scope recommend_or_warn gets close but is not guaranteed for every learner. B2 requires the trade-off stated explicitly (advantage_disadvantage_frame) as its own discourse move, which a real recommendation needs regardless of whether recommend_or_warn was evidenced.
transferContexts: comparing options never used during teaching

canDos.why: Turns a one-sided defense into a real discussion; cheap to add once develop_and_defend_opinion exists, and it multiplies naturally into the capstone's pushback capability.
transferContexts: conceding a point in a novel argument

canDos.why: The reasoning half of a complaint: explaining why a change is warranted, before proposing what the change should be.
transferContexts: justifying a request for a problem type not used during teaching

canDos.why: B1 already required negotiate_a_solution for a single-round, reported problem. B2's escalation is justification-grounded proposals and adjusting across genuine pushback, which is what the capstone's negotiate_an_agreement_under_pushback then tests directly — not a re-teach of B1's negotiation.
transferContexts: negotiating a resolution for a problem type not used during teaching

canDos.why: B1's should-scope express_frustration_politely is a flat-politeness tone layer on report_a_problem. B2 adds hedged, register-aware diplomacy sustained inside a live negotiation with pushback, which is a genuinely new discourse demand, not the same skill renamed.
transferContexts: expressing frustration about a novel problem

canDos.why: B1's should-scope talk_about_real_conditions and optional imagine_a_hypothetical ('a light preview of B2's hypothetical reasoning, kept to one fixed frame') already point here, but neither is required, so this capability's hard prerequisite stays the required b1.talk_about_plans_and_intentions. This is the level's core new grammar-as-thinking-tool capability, and every later hypothesis/regret capability builds on it.
transferContexts: a hypothetical scenario not used during teaching

canDos.why: Reasoning about why something happened or must be true, with calibrated certainty, is the everyday-reasoning complement to explicit hypothesis.
transferContexts: speculating about a novel everyday mystery

canDos.why: The affective, past-facing sibling of hypothesis: saying what they would have done differently, reusing the third-conditional machinery for a genuinely different function.
transferContexts: expressing regret about a novel past decision

canDos.why: B1's should-scope summarize_what_was_said recaps for the same interlocutor, inside the same conversation. B2 requires the genuine CEFR mediation move: a summary for a third party who was not present, which is the first required capability in the curriculum where that bridging act is itself the skill, not a side effect.
transferContexts: summarizing a source text/conversation not used during teaching

canDos.why: Rewording something confusing so a listener actually understands it — the clarity half of mediation, distinct from condensing.
transferContexts: reformulating a passage not used during teaching

canDos.why: Reporting a third person's stance accurately, combining reported speech with recognizing an opinion well enough to relay it.
transferContexts: reporting an opinion not used during teaching

canDos.why: The level's first capability where register/pragmatics is itself the evaluated skill, not incidental — noticing and switching formality to match the relationship and situation.
transferContexts: a register shift not used during teaching

canDos.why: Deliberately modulating a claim's force is the productive complement to noticing register; it reuses the opinion frame from arc 1 under a new lens.
transferContexts: softening/strengthening a claim not used during teaching

canDos.why: The receptive complement to register production: catching a meaning that was implied, not stated, which real conversations constantly require.
transferContexts: an implication not used during teaching

canDos.why: The capstone's first new capability: keeping a conversation going across more than one subject, at the length a real B2 exchange needs.
transferContexts: the entire capstone conversation, by construction

canDos.why: Following and contributing to a topic change instead of forcing the old subject to continue — the specific skill A1 explicitly excludes and B2 must own.
transferContexts: the entire capstone conversation, by construction

canDos.why: The level's integrating capability: recombining concession, negotiation and register-softening under repeated objection, proving recombination rather than new material.
transferContexts: the entire capstone conversation, by construction
canDos.architecturalNote: pushback_response_pattern is deliberately not a new pattern group — it recombines concession_counter_pattern, negotiation_proposal_pattern and diplomatic_hedge_pattern.

canDos.why: Recognition-level idiom exposure inside the capstone, without making idiomatic fluency a required B2 outcome — that is C1/C2 territory.

patterns.form: In my view / I'd argue that / As I see it
whereas / on the other hand / by contrast
the main advantage/drawback of X is that…
that's true, but / I take your point, however
given that / since / the reason I'm asking is that
would you be willing to / what if we / I'd suggest that
I understand, but / I don't want to make a fuss, but
If I were…, I would…
If I had…, I would have…
If I had…, I would… [now]
must be / might be / can't be
must have / might have / could have
I wish I had… / if only I'd…
tense back-shift + claim/mention/point out/suggest
basically / the main point was / to sum up
in other words / what I mean is / put simply
could you possibly (formal) vs can you (informal)
sort of / tend to / I'd say / more or less
absolutely / without a doubt / I'm convinced that
anyway / speaking of which / that reminds me / before I forget

proposed.whyNotExisting: No existing type carries an opinionated position on an issue; a slot that accepts a stance must reject a concrete noun.
A service/plan failure is a categorized situation, not a place, object or feeling; existing types would force an inaccurate substitution.
Register is a property of the relationship/situation's formality, not a concrete slot filler any existing type carries.

explicitlyNotNeeded.why: A debated topic is a context, not a capability or a semantic type — the master contract's rule that topics are contexts, not curriculum (section 6).
Idiomatic expressions are vocabulary items tracked as multiword Garden units, not a slot type; use_idiomatic_expressions_naturally has no productive slot.

intentStrategy.rule: One intent per communicative function; variants travel as a subtype on the step payload, following the rule already applied in A1 (a1-blueprint.json intentStrategy) rather than being reinvented here.

newSubtypesOnExistingIntents.change: pushback subtype used only inside the_long_conversation, where the same intent must be judged across repeated objection rounds rather than once

counts.explosionGuard: If an arc's design needs more than three new intents, the arc is teaching phrases rather than a capability — same rule A1 applied.

evaluationStrategy.rule: Unlike A1, B2 does not claim every capability is designed to require no reachable provider. Open, paragraph-length argumentative and mediation turns are the median case here, not the exception, so the honest three-tier fallback in b2.md section 15.3/15.4 applies: provider-graded when reachable, a declared structural floor when not, with the degraded state surfaced honestly rather than silently accepted or silently downgraded.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can state an opinion with a reason (B1) but cannot sustain it against a real counter-argument, or weigh several options against each other rather than just picking a favorite.
arcs.whyNow: The smallest step from B1's opinion-with-reason, and it introduces the stance/contrast machinery every later arc reuses.

miniStory.why: The arc's value is a genuine two-sided discussion, which roleplay carries better than a narrated scene.

arcs.autonomyTarget: early: frame/connector list visible while stance language is new, withheld on the arc's integrated episode
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided opinion defenses and one unaided trade-off recommendation
arcs.risk: Debate-style content can drift into abstract/academic topics; the budget is spent on concrete, everyday-real issues only.
arcs.episodes: planned, not yet numbered — B2 episode numbering is content-authoring scope

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can describe a problem (B1) but cannot justify a request for a specific change or negotiate toward a resolution with the person responsible.
arcs.whyNow: Reuses arc 1's stance/concession machinery, redirected at a real complaint rather than an abstract opinion.

miniStory.why: A negotiation has a beginning, an obstacle and a resolution — a hosted scene can carry the other party's turns while the learner keeps the decisions.

arcs.autonomyTarget: early-to-mid: proposal frame visible while new, withheld once negotiation is reused in the arc's integrated episode
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided negotiation proposals and one unaided justified request, transferred to a problem type not taught
arcs.risk: Negotiation content can read as scripted haggling; the risk mitigation is grounding every scenario in a real service/booking/order failure.
arcs.episodes: planned, not yet numbered — B2 episode numbering is content-authoring scope

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner cannot yet reason about an unreal present/future, speculate about cause and effect with calibrated certainty, or express regret about a past decision.
arcs.whyNow: Independent of arcs 1-2 (only needs B1 exit); the level's steepest new grammar earns its own arc rather than being folded into another.

miniStory.why: An everyday mystery (a missing package, a locked door) gives speculation a genuine reason to happen rather than being an isolated grammar drill.

arcs.autonomyTarget: early: heaviest support of any arc given six new pattern groups; fades only after each conditional form is independently produced once
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided hypotheses, two unaided speculations, one unaided expression of regret
arcs.risk: The level's densest arc: six new pattern groups. Mitigated by teaching second-conditional before third-conditional before mixed, each reusing the last.
arcs.episodes: planned, not yet numbered — B2 episode numbering is content-authoring scope

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner cannot summarize a conversation or text for somebody who was not there, reword something confusing into something clear, or report a third person's opinion accurately.
arcs.whyNow: Independent of arcs 1-3 (only needs B1 exit); mediation is the first capability family in the curriculum where processing someone else's language for a third party is itself the required skill.

miniStory.why: Mediation needs authentic-feeling source material (a conversation or short text) to process, which a hosted scene supplies better than a roleplay alone.

arcs.autonomyTarget: mid: connector list visible while reformulating is new; withheld once summarizing is reused for reporting
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided summaries, two unaided reformulations, one unaided accurate report of an opinion
arcs.risk: Meaning-preservation is the hardest thing to grade honestly offline (section 15.4); the arc's design leans on provider-preferred evaluation with a declared structural floor, never a false claim of verified accuracy.
arcs.episodes: planned, not yet numbered — B2 episode numbering is content-authoring scope

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner cannot yet notice or switch register to match a relationship/situation, deliberately soften or strengthen a claim, or catch an implication that was not stated outright.
arcs.whyNow: Needs an opinion to modulate, so it follows making_the_case; register work is meaningless without something to say more or less formally.

miniStory.why: The same problem told to a landlord and to a flatmate is best shown as two parallel short scenes, so the register contrast is directly comparable.

arcs.autonomyTarget: mid: register markers visible while new; the arc's integrated episode withholds them and requires a self-initiated register choice
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided register adjustments, two unaided hedge/intensify productions, one unaided correct inference of implied meaning
arcs.risk: Register is the level's most invisible skill to a learner who does not ask for help; scaffolding must surface it explicitly rather than assuming it will be noticed.
arcs.episodes: planned, not yet numbered — B2 episode numbering is content-authoring scope

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can do each B2 function alone but has not yet sustained all of them together across a long, multi-topic, spontaneous exchange that ends in a real agreement.
arcs.whyNow: Last, because it needs every preceding arc at once and introduces almost nothing of its own — the same design logic as A1's closing arrangement arc.
arcs.neutralFallback: a shared-flat dispute requiring a plan, a complaint, a compromise and a topic change to logistics

miniStory.why: The level's closing situation: an extended, realistic negotiation with genuine topic changes, functioning as the level's delayed-retrieval instrument for every prior arc.

arcs.autonomyTarget: late: unaided by default; support returns only after a strained turn
arcs.evidenceTarget: the three new capstone capabilities each produced twice unaided, plus at least one delayed-retrieval instance of every arc 1-5 required capability
arcs.risk: Could become a review episode with a new label. It earns its place only if the learner leaves able to hold a real, unscripted, multi-topic negotiation nobody rehearsed verbatim.
arcs.episodes: planned, not yet numbered — B2 episode numbering is content-authoring scope

reuseMatrix.b1RowsNote: b1.* prerequisite reuse (give_an_opinion, compare_options_with_reasons, negotiate_a_solution, sustain_topic_change, narrate_connected_event, talk_about_plans_and_intentions) is not tabulated here because their arc-by-arc B1 reuse pattern is owned by b1.md/b1.json, not by this file — cross-checked in LC-AUD-001.

coreEngineRequirements.problem: Judge whether a turn coherently continues a multi-turn exchange, not only whether it matches a canonical per-turn intent frame.
coreEngineRequirements.earliestLevel: b1 (light version arguably needed already); b2 is first to require actual evaluation of it
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: low for A1/Pre-A1/B1 single-topic short exchanges

coreEngineRequirements.problem: Grade a semantically/grammatically correct reply as register-inappropriate for its context, as a separate verdict from the semantic one.
coreEngineRequirements.earliestLevel: b2 (arc 5, the capstone); c1 generalizes it per the master contract
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: none if additive and defaulting to not_applicable

coreEngineRequirements.problem: Grade open, paragraph-length argumentative/negotiation turns honestly when the provider is unreachable, without silently downgrading the task or silently accepting anything.
coreEngineRequirements.earliestLevel: b2 (first level where such turns are the median case, not the exception)
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: none to earlier levels, which keep fully local evaluation

coreEngineRequirements.problem: Judge whether a reworded sentence/summary preserves a source text's meaning, distinct from matching a canonical target frame.
coreEngineRequirements.earliestLevel: b2 (arc 4, first mediation-as-capability arc in the curriculum)
